response:
## CRP Use for Stratification in the Protocol

CRP was considered for stratification in an **earlier version** of the protocol (Version 1.0), but was **removed** in the updated Version 1.1.

### Version 1.0 (Original)
In the original protocol, randomisation stratification included **elevated (≥3 mg/L) CRP levels** as one of the stratification factors: *"90 patients will be centrally, dynamically, stratified randomly (by elevated (≥3 mg/L) CRP levels, and stable conventional treatment (prior treatment with amino salicylates, corticosteroids, and immunosuppressive drugs)) assigned to 3 groups (1:1:1)"* (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 92).

### Version 1.1 (Revised — Current)
In the updated protocol, CRP-based stratification was **replaced**. Randomisation is now stratified by:
1. **Prior corticosteroids treatment (yes/no)**
2. **Consent to participate in PK substudy (yes/no)**

This is confirmed across multiple sections of the protocol: *"Randomisation will be stratified by prior corticosteroids treatment (yes/no) and consent to participate in PK substudy (yes/no)"* (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 8; p. 26; p. 36).

### CRP as an Exploratory Biomarker
Although CRP is no longer used as a stratification factor, it is still assessed as an **exploratory endpoint** — specifically, change from Baseline to Weeks 4, 8, and 12 in CRP is measured (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 7). CRP is analysed at **local sites** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 45).

### Summary
| Version | CRP Role in Stratification |
|---|---|
| V1.0 | Used: elevated CRP ≥3 mg/L as stratification factor |
| V1.1 (current) | Removed from stratification; retained only as exploratory biomarker |

response:
## Planned Safety Analyses

The following safety analyses are planned for this trial:

### 1. General Approach
- Safety analyses will be **summarized descriptively by treatment groups** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 13)
- **No statistical testing** for comparison of treatment groups will be performed for safety variables (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 13 & p. 68)
- All statistical analyses will be detailed in a separate **Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP)** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 66)

### 2. Safety Analysis Set
- The Safety Analysis Set will include **all randomised patients who received at least one dose of IMP**, with treatment assignment according to actual treatment received (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 67)

### 3. Safety Parameters Evaluated
Complete data listings and summary tables will be created for all safety information, including:
- **Adverse events**
- **Concomitant medications**
- **Vital signs**
- **Clinical laboratory test values**
- **12-lead ECG** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 68)

### 4. Baseline Definition
- For safety data, **Baseline is defined as the last observed value collected prior to the start of treatment** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 68)

### 5. Safety Review Committee (SRC)
- A **Safety Review Committee (SRC)** will be established to periodically review cumulative safety data at regular intervals
- The SRC will review **blinded data** and provide recommendations to the Sponsor
- The SRC will comprise **at least a medical monitor, a physician, and a pharmacologist**
- Responsibilities include evaluating safety concerns and making recommendations regarding trial conduct and possible trial modifications (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 29)

response:
Based on the protocol, the following fields and information should be included in the e-CRF:

## Adverse Event Log
Each adverse event entry must include (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 58):
- Adverse event description
- Date of onset (time can be recorded, if applicable)
- Intensity
- Causal relationship to IMP
- Action taken to IMP
- Other action taken
- Date and time of outcome
- Outcome
- Seriousness

## Screening & Enrollment Data
- Selected data for screened patients, including reason for screening failure if the patient is not randomised (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 36)

## Concomitant Medications
- Details of all concomitant medication along with the main reason for prescription
- Prior treatment for UC within 12 months of Visit 1 (Screening) (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 37)

## Withdrawal / Discontinuation
- Date of premature termination
- Main reason for discontinuation
- If discontinuation is due to an adverse event, the specific event must be recorded (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 38)

## SAE Reporting
The following are mandatory for initial and follow-up SAE reports (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 63):
- Demographics
- Adverse Event Log
- Medical History Log
- Concomitant Medication Log

## Unscheduled Visits
- Description of the unscheduled visit including the reason for the visit (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 52)

## Protocol Deviations
- Documentation of any deviation, including description, relevant dates (start and stop), and action taken (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 75)

## Additional Documents Stored Alongside the e-CRF
The following should be stored with hospital/medical records or the Investigator File (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 71):
- Laboratory print-outs (central and local)
- ECG print-outs/reports
- Patient dispensing logs of IMP
- Evaluations of physical assessments

> **Note:** The protocol references additional e-CRF fields but the excerpt for physical evaluations is cut off (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 71). Full details of all e-CRF fields beyond those listed above — such as specific visit data fields, vital signs, or efficacy assessments — I don't have this information from the provided context.

response:
Based on the provided protocol documents, **I don't have this information**. The documents do not specify any maximum lifetime cumulative dose of TJ301 across multiple trials.

The documents do provide the following related dosing information for the current trial only:

- The maximum dose within **this specific trial** is **600 mg Q2W** for 12 consecutive weeks, totalling **6 doses** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p32)
- In the prior **Phase 1 study**, the maximum dose was **600 mg weekly for 4 consecutive weeks** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p32)
- The dose range investigated across Phase 1 studies was **0.75 mg to 750 mg** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p23)

No language regarding lifetime cumulative dosing limits across multiple trials is present in the provided context.
